## Fact Check: Current COVID-19 Vaccines Do Not Contain Graphene Oxide

Claims circulating online and on social media platforms falsely assert that current COVID-19 vaccines contain graphene oxide. These claims, which have gained traction across various online communities, are demonstrably false and lack any scientific basis.

Independent fact-checking organizations and scientific experts have repeatedly debunked this misinformation. No evidence supports the presence of graphene oxide in the composition of any of the COVID-19 vaccines currently authorized for use globally. Thorough analyses and official ingredient lists released by vaccine manufacturers, such as Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna, and Johnson & Johnson, consistently omit graphene oxide. These ingredient lists are readily available and accessible to the public on the manufacturers' websites and through official regulatory bodies like the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA).

The spread of this misinformation has been fueled by a combination of unsubstantiated claims, misinterpreted research, and a general distrust of established scientific and medical institutions. Certain individuals and groups have presented analyses, often lacking scientific rigor, that falsely suggest the presence of graphene oxide based on misinterpreted microscopy images or flawed interpretations of scientific data.

It is crucial to rely on credible sources of information regarding vaccine composition and safety. Public health officials and scientific experts are working diligently to combat misinformation and ensure that the public has access to accurate and reliable information about COVID-19 vaccines. Individuals encountering claims about graphene oxide in vaccines should consult official sources like the CDC, WHO, and reputable news organizations specializing in science and health reporting.

## Digital Vaccination Certificates: Ministry of Health Remains the Only Valid Authority in Colombia

A recent trend involving digital copies of physical vaccination certificates has sparked discussion in Colombia. While some websites offer to create digital duplicates of the yellow card traditionally used to prove vaccination status, it's crucial to remember that the only officially recognized and valid vaccination certificate in Colombia remains the one issued directly by the Ministry of Health.

The physical yellow card, often provided at the point of vaccination, has long been the accepted method of proof. However, the digital age has naturally led to exploration of electronic alternatives. The appeal of a digital version is clear: convenience, reduced risk of loss or damage, and ease of sharing. Several websites are now capitalizing on this demand by offering to create digital reproductions of the information contained on the physical card.

The concern, however, lies in the legal validity and acceptance of these independently generated digital copies. According to official statements and regulations, only the vaccination certificates issued by the Ministry of Health hold official weight. This is because the Ministry maintains the national vaccination registry and is the sole authority responsible for verifying and validating vaccination data within the country.

While a digital copy generated by a third-party website may accurately reflect the information on the physical card, it lacks the official endorsement and authentication of the Ministry. Therefore, using such a copy as a substitute for the official Ministry-issued certificate could potentially lead to issues when proof of vaccination is required, such as for travel, access to certain events, or other regulated activities.

It is important for individuals in Colombia to understand the distinction between a personal digital copy and the official vaccination certificate. While creating a digital backup of your physical card may be a useful organizational tool, it should not be considered a substitute for the official documentation issued by the Ministry of Health. Always rely on the official certificate for any situation where proof of vaccination is required. Further information and updates regarding official vaccination certificates can be found on the Ministry of Health's website.

## Israel Faces New COVID-19 Surge Amid Delta Variant Spread and Misinformation

Israel, a nation lauded for its early and rapid COVID-19 vaccination program, is currently experiencing a new surge in cases. This increase has been linked to the prevalence of the Delta variant and a simultaneous relaxation of public health measures. While the efficacy of vaccines against infection has been a key topic of discussion globally, the situation in Israel highlights the complex interplay of factors influencing pandemic control.

The surge has raised concerns, especially as it affects even vaccinated individuals. While vaccines remain highly effective at preventing severe illness, hospitalization, and death, their ability to prevent all infections appears to be somewhat diminished against the Delta variant. This has led to renewed debate regarding booster shots and the continued importance of non-pharmaceutical interventions like mask-wearing and social distancing, even in highly vaccinated populations.

However, the real story has become muddied by the spread of misinformation. The website Trikooba recently published an article leveraging data surrounding the recent surge in Israel to spread misleading information about mRNA vaccines. The article reportedly exploits the anxieties surrounding breakthrough infections and the evolving understanding of the Delta variant's impact.

This misuse of data underscores a critical challenge in the ongoing fight against COVID-19: the need to combat the spread of inaccurate and misleading information. Even as scientific understanding of the virus and the effectiveness of vaccines evolves, the proliferation of false narratives can undermine public trust in established medical consensus and hinder efforts to protect public health. It is crucial for individuals to rely on credible sources of information and to critically evaluate the claims presented, especially when dealing with complex scientific data. The situation in Israel serves as a stark reminder of the potential for misinformation to complicate an already challenging public health crisis.

இந்த தரவு பயன்பாடு விவாதத்தின் போது சர்வதேச விபத்துக்களுக்கு எதிராக நடவடிக்கை எடுக்கும் தொடர்பில் ஒரு முக்கிய சவாலாக இருக்கிறது: தவறான தகவல்களின் பரவலை தடுத்து நிறுத்துவது. விரைவாக விபத்துக்களும் மருந்துகளின் திறனும் விவரங்களை புரிந்து கொள்வது மற்றும் விவரங்கள் பற்றிய அறிவு வளர்வது என்பது முக்கியமாக இருக்கிறது. ஆனால், தவறான கருத்துகள் பரவலாக இருந்தால், அது தற்போது இருக்கும் சிக்கலான சுகாதார போராட்டத்தை மேலும் சிக்கலாக்கலாம். மேலும், கோவிட்-19 தொடர்பான தகவல்களை பொருத்த சரியான தரவு வளையத்தில் பொருத்துவது மற்றும் சிக்கலான விஞ்ஞான விவரங்கள் குறித்து கருத்துகளை ஆராய்வது மிகவும் முக்கியமானது. இஸ்ரேலில் நிகழும் நிலை தற்போது பரவியுள்ள தவறான தகவல்கள் மூலம் சுகாதார போராட்டத்தை சிக்கலாக்கும் அபாயத்தை விளக்குகிறது.

## Coronavirus Variants Emerged Before Vaccine Rollout, Data Suggests

Documented samples of novel coronavirus variants were collected and studied prior to the commencement of COVID-19 vaccination programs globally, according to research indicating the virus was evolving and mutating even before widespread immunity efforts began. These findings highlight the inherent nature of viruses to change and adapt, and underscore the importance of continuous monitoring and surveillance in combating infectious diseases.

While the exact timeline and prevalence of these early variants remain under investigation, their identification before vaccination efforts kicked off is significant. It reinforces the understanding that the COVID-19 virus was not a static entity and that changes were occurring even in the early stages of the pandemic.

The primary association of these early viral changes, as noted in the research, is linked to the virus's ability to spread. This implies that these initial mutations likely conferred an advantage in transmission, potentially allowing the virus to become more infectious and reach a wider population. This aligns with the broader understanding of viral evolution, where mutations that enhance transmissibility are often favored and can contribute to the dominance of new variants.

The implications of this information are multifaceted. Firstly, it underscores the need for robust genomic surveillance programs to track and understand the evolution of viruses in real-time. By monitoring these changes, public health officials can better anticipate potential surges, adapt testing strategies, and tailor public health interventions accordingly. Secondly, it emphasizes the crucial role of continued research into understanding the impact of specific mutations on viral characteristics such as transmissibility, virulence, and vaccine effectiveness.

Understanding the evolutionary trajectory of the COVID-19 virus, from its earliest documented forms to the emergence of more recent variants, remains a crucial element in informing public health policies and mitigating the ongoing impact of the pandemic. Continued surveillance and research are essential to anticipate future viral changes and ensure that interventions remain effective.

## Catholic Group Circulates Misinformation About Vaccines Through Leaflet Campaign

A Catholic organization is under scrutiny for distributing leaflets containing misinformation about vaccines, raising concerns among public health officials and religious scholars. The leaflet, which has been circulating online, reportedly relies on unsubstantiated claims and questionable arguments to discourage vaccination.

The distribution of these leaflets highlights a persistent challenge in combating vaccine hesitancy: the spread of misinformation within specific communities. Targeting religious groups with inaccurate information about vaccines can be particularly damaging, as faith leaders and community networks often hold significant influence.

The content of the leaflet, according to sources who have seen it, centers on scientifically discredited concerns about vaccine safety and efficacy. These concerns may include claims about vaccine ingredients, purported links to autism (a long-debunked claim), and arguments against the necessity of vaccination, often presented within a religious framework.

The emergence of this leaflet underscores the ongoing need for robust public health communication strategies, particularly those tailored to address the specific concerns of different communities. Collaboration between public health experts, religious leaders, and trusted community members is crucial to counter misinformation and promote accurate information about vaccines. By fostering open dialogue and addressing concerns with evidence-based information, it may be possible to build trust and encourage informed decision-making regarding vaccination. This leaflet serves as a reminder of the constant vigilance needed to protect vulnerable populations from the dangers of health misinformation.

## Understanding the Devastating Flu of 1918 and the Distinct Threat of Meningitis

The influenza pandemic of 1918, a global catastrophe that claimed an estimated 50 to 100 million lives, serves as a stark reminder of the devastating potential of viral outbreaks. Often referred to as the "Spanish Flu," this pandemic, which unfolded over several waves, was a significantly more virulent strain than typical seasonal influenza. Scientific consensus now points to the H1N1 virus as the causative agent, tracing its origins back to avian sources.

The identification of the H1N1 virus as the culprit behind the 1918 pandemic was a major breakthrough in understanding the disease. Researchers have been able to reconstruct the virus and study its behavior, helping to inform our preparedness for future influenza pandemics. Understanding the avian origin highlights the ongoing importance of monitoring avian influenza strains and their potential for transmission to humans. The flu virus is known for its ability to mutate and jump between species, making constant surveillance a critical element of global health security.

Contrastingly, meningitis is a distinct illness caused by bacteria. Unlike influenza, which is caused by a virus and primarily affects the respiratory system, meningitis is an inflammation of the membranes (meninges) surrounding the brain and spinal cord. While viral meningitis exists, bacterial meningitis is generally more severe and can lead to serious complications, including brain damage, hearing loss, and even death.

Various bacteria can cause meningitis, including *Streptococcus pneumoniae* and *Neisseria meningitidis*. These bacteria can spread through close contact, such as coughing, sneezing, or sharing utensils. Prompt diagnosis and treatment with antibiotics are crucial to combat bacterial meningitis and minimize its potential for long-term effects.

The distinction between the 1918 flu and meningitis underscores the importance of understanding the diverse range of pathogens that can cause widespread illness and death. While both pose serious threats, their origins, modes of transmission, and treatment strategies differ significantly. Public health efforts must address both viral and bacterial threats with tailored prevention and response measures to safeguard global health.

Despite a slowdown in demand leading to the closure of some vaccination centers, the national COVID-19 vaccination program remains active in a European country. This could involve shifting resources to mobile vaccination units, pharmacies, or general practitioner offices to reach individuals who may have difficulty accessing larger centers.

The ongoing vaccination program indicates a continued commitment to mitigating the impact of COVID-19 within the nation. While the urgency of the initial phase has diminished, health officials are likely emphasizing the importance of staying up-to-date with vaccinations, particularly for vulnerable groups like the elderly and those with underlying health conditions. ## Debunking Claims of Graphene and Altered Blood Color in COVID-19 Vaccines

Social media is currently circulating an image depicting two bags of blood, noticeably different in color, being used to suggest that COVID-19 vaccines contain graphene and that vaccination alters the color of a person's blood. However, these claims are unsubstantiated and lack scientific evidence.

The assertion that COVID-19 vaccines contain graphene has been widely debunked by scientific and medical experts. Regulatory agencies worldwide, including the World Health Organization (WHO), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States, and the European Medicines Agency (EMA), have rigorously reviewed the composition of these vaccines. None of these reviews have found any evidence of graphene or graphene-based materials being used as ingredients. The publicly available ingredient lists of all approved COVID-19 vaccines confirm this.

Furthermore, the claim that vaccination changes the color of a person's blood is scientifically unfounded. Blood color varies depending on its oxygen saturation. Arterial blood, which is rich in oxygen, is typically bright red. Venous blood, which has less oxygen, is a darker red, sometimes appearing almost purplish. These variations are completely normal physiological processes and are not influenced by vaccination.

The visual presented in the image likely depicts blood samples collected or stored under different conditions, leading to the variation in color. Factors such as the anticoagulant used, the length of storage, and even the individual's hydration levels can influence the appearance of blood samples. Without understanding the context of the image and the origin of the blood samples, it is impossible to draw any legitimate conclusions about the impact of vaccination.

Spreading misinformation about vaccines can erode public trust and undermine efforts to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. It is crucial to rely on credible sources of information, such as public health authorities and peer-reviewed scientific research, when evaluating claims about vaccine safety and efficacy. Before sharing information online, especially when it relates to health, it is important to verify its accuracy with reliable and trusted sources.

## Десенсування тверджень про графен та зміну кольору крові в вакцинах проти Ковід-19

Соціальні мережі заздалегідь розповсюджують зображення, на якому зображено дві сумки крові, що значно відрізняються за кольором, щоб посилатися на те, що вакцини проти Ковід-19 містять графен, а вакцинація змінює колір крові людини. Однак ці твердження не мають підстав і відсутні наукові докази.

Твердження про те, що вакцини проти Ковід-19 містять графен, широко відкинуто науковцями та лікарями. Повсюдні регуляторні організації, включаючи Всесвітню організацію охорони здоров'я (ВООЗ), Центральний центр контролю за хворобами та профілактики (CDC) в США та Європейську агенцію ліків (ЕМА), докладно перевірили склад цих вакцин. Ніяких доказів використання графену або матеріалів, побудованих на графені, як компонентів не знайдено. Публічно доступні списки компонентів усіх затверджених вакцин проти Ковід-19 підтверджують це.

Крім того, твердження про те, що вакцинація змінює колір крові людини, науково не має підстав. Колір крові залежить від її насыщеності киснем. Артеріальна кров, що багата киснем, зазвичай має яскраво-червоний колір, а венозна кров, що містить менше кисню, має темно-червоний колір, іноді набуваючи майже фіолетового вигляду. Ці варіації є повністю нормальними фізіологічними процесами і не впливають на вакцинацію.

Зображення, подане в соціальних мережах, ймовірно, відображає кров'яну плазму, зібрану або зберігану у різних умовах, що призводить до різниці в колорі. Фактори, такі як використання антикоагулюючого засобу, тривалість зберігання та навіть гідратація особи, можуть впливати на зовнішній вигляд кров'яних проб. Без урахування контексту зображення та походження кров'яних проб неможливо зробити будь-які обґрунтовані висновки про вплив вакцинації.

Розповсюдження неправдивої інформації про вакцини може знищити довіру суспільства та зруйнувати зусилля, спрямовані на боротьбу з пандемією Ковід-19. Важливо залежати від достовірних джерел інформації, таких як державні органи охорони здоров'я та наукові дослідження, які проходять рецензування, при оцінці тверджень про безпеку та ефективність вакцин. Перед поширенням інформації, особливо щодо здоров'я, важливо перевіряти її точність з надійних та довірених джерел.

## Misinformation Spreads After Antivax Entrepreneur Misrepresents FDA Stance

A wave of misinformation is circulating online after an antivaccine entrepreneur misrepresented the stance of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) during a recent FDA event. The false claim, now widely shared across social media platforms, is falsely attributed to the FDA itself.

The incident highlights the ongoing challenges of combating the spread of inaccurate information regarding vaccines and public health. While details of the specific event are still emerging, it is confirmed that an individual, identified as an antivaccine entrepreneur, made the disputed statement while attending a gathering related to the FDA.

It's crucial to understand that the FDA is responsible for regulating and supervising the safety of food, pharmaceuticals, and medical devices in the United States. Its decisions are based on scientific evidence and rigorous testing protocols. Therefore, attributing an unsupported and potentially dangerous claim to the agency is not only inaccurate but also undermines public trust in a vital regulatory body.

The spread of this misinformation underscores the power of social media to amplify false narratives. In a climate already polarized by debates surrounding vaccination, such claims can have serious consequences, potentially influencing individuals to make decisions that negatively impact their health and the health of their communities.

Fact-checking organizations are actively working to debunk the false claim and clarify the FDA's official position. Consumers are urged to verify information from trusted sources, such as the FDA website (fda.gov) or reputable news outlets, before sharing it online. It is essential to remain vigilant and critical of information encountered on social media, particularly when it relates to health and medical advice. Further investigation into the event and the individual involved is expected to shed more light on the motivation and intent behind this instance of misinformation.

## Lawsuit Against Scientist Over Ivermectin Tweet Dismissed in Mumbai Court

A lawsuit filed against a scientist in Mumbai, India, alleging misinformation regarding ivermectin, has been dismissed by a court. The suit, initiated by a law firm, centered around claims that the scientist misled Indian citizens by failing to recommend the use of the drug in a tweet.

The legal challenge stemmed from the widespread and, in many cases, controversial use of ivermectin as a potential treatment for COVID-19 during the pandemic. While some promoted the drug as a viable option, scientific consensus largely rejected its efficacy against the virus, citing a lack of robust evidence from clinical trials. Major health organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), did not recommend its use for COVID-19.

The basis of the lawsuit appears to be rooted in the differing opinions and debates surrounding ivermectin’s potential benefits. The claimants, represented by the law firm, argued that the scientist's tweet, by omitting a recommendation for ivermectin, actively misled the Indian public. This suggests the plaintiffs believed the scientist had a responsibility to promote, or at least acknowledge, the drug as a possible treatment, despite the prevailing scientific opinion questioning its effectiveness.

The court's dismissal of the case indicates that the judge found the plaintiff’s arguments unconvincing and likely ruled that the scientist's tweet did not constitute actionable misinformation. The specifics of the court’s reasoning remain unclear based on available information, but it likely considered the established scientific understanding of ivermectin's role in COVID-19 treatment, and the right to express opinions within the bounds of responsible discourse. The case highlights the complex and often contentious nature of scientific debate within the public sphere, particularly during times of crisis, and the challenges in balancing freedom of speech with concerns about the spread of misinformation.

article_summary: Un abogado en Mumbai presentó una demanda contra un científico por supuestamente difundir información falsa sobre el ivermectin en una publicación, pero el caso fue desestimado. La controversia surge de la disputa sobre el uso del medicamento como posible tratamiento para el COVID-19, mientras que organismos como la OMS y la FDA no lo recomiendan. El juez consideró que la publicación no constituyó difamación, priorizando el derecho a la opinión científica frente a la presión por promover tratamientos no validados.
post_content: En realidad, fue una denuncia presentada por un bufete de abogados en un tribunal de Bombay, pero fue desestimada. Los demandantes alegaron que el científico, en un tuit, había engañado a los ciudadanos indios al no recomendar el uso de ivermectina.

## Misinterpretation Fuels Vaccine Effectiveness Claims

Claims circulating online regarding the ineffectiveness of vaccinations have been linked to a misinterpretation of a recent study's results. The inaccurate conclusion, which has gained traction on social media platforms, stems from a flawed understanding of the data presented, according to experts familiar with the research.

While the specific study being cited hasn't been explicitly named by those propagating the misinformation, the core issue lies in the misapplication or simplification of statistical findings. Studies on vaccine effectiveness often present nuanced data regarding efficacy against different variants, severity of illness, or durations of protection. ## Marburg Virus: Remembering a Past Outbreak and Looking Ahead

In 1967, a novel virus emerged, leaving a lasting impact on the scientific community and public health landscape. This virus, later identified as the Marburg virus, was first detected following an outbreak traced back to laboratory workers in Marburg and Frankfurt, Germany. The initial cases highlighted the virus's zoonotic origin, with exposure linked to infected African green monkeys used in laboratory research.

The defining characteristic of Marburg virus disease (MVD) is its propensity to cause severe hemorrhagic fever. The illness typically begins abruptly with fever, headache, and malaise. As the disease progresses, patients often experience muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. The most alarming symptom is the development of severe hemorrhaging, both internal and external, which can lead to organ failure and death.

While the 1967 outbreak brought the Marburg virus to international attention, subsequent outbreaks have occurred primarily in Africa. These outbreaks, often smaller in scale but devastating in their impact, serve as a constant reminder of the virus's potential to emerge and cause significant morbidity and mortality.

In August 2021, the World Health Organization (WHO) addressed a renewed concern with a confirmed outbreak of Marburg virus in Guinea, West Africa. This outbreak, though localized, prompted immediate response efforts from international health organizations to contain the spread of the virus and provide support to affected communities. The WHO's involvement underscores the seriousness with which Marburg is regarded within the global health community, and emphasizes the importance of proactive surveillance and rapid response mechanisms in preventing larger outbreaks.

The Marburg virus, while rare, poses a significant public health threat due to its high mortality rate and potential for rapid spread. Ongoing research and preparedness efforts are crucial for developing effective treatments and prevention strategies to combat future outbreaks of this deadly virus. Understanding the history and epidemiology of Marburg is essential for mitigating its impact and protecting global health security.

## Debunking Viral Claims: Vaccines Don't Alter DNA, and a Video of a Premature Infant is Not "Transhuman"

Social media platforms are rife with misinformation, and recent claims surrounding COVID-19 vaccines and a viral video of a newborn are prime examples. Online users have been falsely asserting that COVID-19 vaccines can alter a person's DNA and that a circulating video depicts a "transhuman" baby. These claims are demonstrably false and lack any scientific basis.

The assertion that COVID-19 vaccines modify DNA is a dangerous and misleading myth that has been repeatedly debunked by scientists and medical experts worldwide. COVID-19 vaccines, including mRNA vaccines, work by introducing a set of instructions to our cells, triggering an immune response that prepares the body to fight the virus. These instructions are temporary and do not interact with or alter our DNA. The mRNA never enters the nucleus of the cell, where DNA resides, making such modification impossible.

Furthermore, a video currently circulating on social media platforms that purports to show a "transhuman" newborn is also false. Investigations have revealed that the video actually depicts a premature infant receiving medical care in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). The child's appearance and the surrounding equipment are consistent with standard medical procedures for premature babies requiring specialized care.

Spreading misinformation about vaccines and depicting vulnerable individuals in a false light can have serious consequences. The proliferation of such content can erode public trust in science and medicine, discourage vaccination efforts, and cause unnecessary distress to the families of individuals featured in misleading videos.

It is crucial for social media users to critically evaluate the information they encounter online, consult reliable sources such as public health organizations and scientific institutions, and refrain from sharing unsubstantiated claims. Verifying information before sharing it can help prevent the spread of misinformation and promote a more informed public discourse.

## Rozprawianie z nieprawdziwymi zarzutami: wakciny przeciwko koronawirusowi nie zmieniają DNA, a wideo noworodka nie przedstawia „transhumanistycznego” dziecka

Platformy społecznościowe są pełne nieprawdziwych informacji, a ostatnie zarzuty dotyczące wakcyn przeciwko koronawirusowi i wideo noworodka stanowią doskonały przykład. Użytkownicy internetowi błędnie twierdzą, że wakcyny przeciwko koronawirusowi mogą zmieniać DNA człowieka, a obiegane wideo przedstawia „transhumanistyczne” dziecko. Te zarzuty są jawnie fałszywe i brak mają podstawy naukowej.

Zarzut, że wakcyny przeciwko koronawirusowi zmieniają DNA, to niebezpieczna i mylna mit, który wielokrotnie został rozeprawiony przez naukowców i specjalistów medycznych na całym świecie. Wakcyny przeciwko koronawirusowi, w tym wakciny mRNA, działają poprzez wprowadzenie zestawu instrukcji do komórek, co wywołuje odpowiedź immunologiczną przygotowującą organizm na walkę z wirusem. Te instrukcje są tymczasowe i nie interagują ani nie zmieniają DNA. mRNA nigdy nie wchodzi do jądra komórki, gdzie znajduje się DNA, co czyni taki zmiany niemożliwym.

Z drugiej strony, obiegane wideo na platformach społecznościowych, które twierdzi, że przedstawia „transhumanistyczne” dziecko, również jest fałszywe. Badania wykazały, że wideo przedstawia w rzeczywistości noworodka wczesnego urodzenia otrzymującego opiekę medyczną w oddziale terapii intensywnej noworodków (NICU). Wygląd dziecka i otaczającego je sprzętu są zgodne z standardowymi procedurami medycznymi dla wczesnie urodzonych dzieci wymagających specjalistycznej opieki.

Rozpowszechnianie nieprawdziwych informacji o wakcjach i przedstawianie wrażliwych osób w nieprawdziwym świetle może mieć poważne konsekwencje. Rozprzestrzenianie się takiego treści może zniszczyć zaufanie społeczeństwa do nauki i medycyny, hamować działania wakcyjne oraz powodować niepotrzebne cierpienie rodziców osób wskazanych w nieprawdziwych wideo.

Ważne jest, by użytkownicy platform społecznościowych krytycznie oceniać informacje, które spotykają na sieci, konsultować się z zaufanymi źródłami takimi jak organizacje zdrowia publicznego i instytucje naukowe oraz unikać rozpowszechniania nieudowodnionych zarzutów. Weryfikacja informacji przed ich udostępnieniem może pomóc zapobiec rozprzestrzenianiu się nieprawdy i wspierać bardziej świadome dyskusje społeczne.
article_summary: Las redes sociales se propagan falsas afirmaciones sobre vacunas de COVID-19 y un video de un bebé prematuro etiquetado como "transhumano". Se desmiente que las vacunas modifiquen el ADN, ya que las vacunas de ARN mensajero no interactúan con el núcleo celular. El video en cuestión muestra a un recién nacido en cuidados intensivos, no a un "transhumano". La desinformación puede erosionar la confianza en la ciencia y generar daño a familias.
